notes: Tests the credibility and method of NRW's Special Area of Conservation phosphate compliance assessments, and how a single outlier sample can drive development restrictions; check the assessment method and how the 2027 reassessment will use Environment Agency data.
summary: In July 2026 a Wrexham County Borough Council planning report found that a single high phosphorus sample taken in March 2025 had kept the Lower Dee classed as failing its target, while Environment Agency samples showed acceptable levels; more than 100 planning applications had been on hold for five years over phosphates. A councillor accused NRW of professional ineptitude and called for it to be broken up. NRW said councils, not NRW, decided to pause applications, that it had recommended the waterbody would not require nutrient neutrality, and that its next River Dee assessment was scheduled for 2027.
title: Wrexham councillors attack NRW over a single Lower Dee phosphate sample that held more than 100 planning applications; NRW drops the nutrient neutrality requirement
